summary: End-user ephemeral tokens being double-counted against org and user buckets causing 429s for NimbleDocs
description:
Issue summary:
NimbleDocs reports repeated 429 responses for end-users during sustained interactive sessions. The customer upgraded to per-user ephemeral tokens to enforce end-user quotas on top of their org-level subscription. Console shows both user and org quota available, but API requests are being throttled.

Impact:
A subset of end-users receive 429s during high-concurrency workflows (document preview + realtime summarization). Customer-facing sessions degrade; several users report timeouts and retries. No full org outage but user-level UX severely impacted.

Environment:
Dedicated account on prod (us-east-1). Using Redwood SDKs with ephemeral tokens minted by customer auth service. Tokens have TTL of 15 minutes. Traffic peak simulated at ~120 concurrent end-users per org.

Observed behavior:
- Requests using ephemeral token appear to be consumed from both the per-user bucket and the org-level tenant bucket simultaneously.
- Console shows user bucket with headroom while tenant bucket is exhausted (429s returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0).
- Throttles occur even though console recently reflected a billing upgrade that should have increased tenant quota.

Expected behavior:
- Ephemeral tokens minted for end-users should be charged only to the intended bucket (user-level) and counted against the org pool per configured policy, not double-counted.

Additional notes:
- Customer moved to ephemeral tokens last week and rotated parent API key on 2026-03-11.
- They use a token-creation service that attaches metadata headers to identify parent_key_id and user_id.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a dedicated account with org API key and enable per-user ephemeral tokens.
2) Use NimbleDocs token minting flow to request ephemeral tokens (TTL 15m).
3) Start 100+ concurrent short-lived streaming sessions using ephemeral tokens.
4) Observe 429s and check response headers for X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Scope.
5) Compare console quota readouts for user and tenant during the spike.

Reproduction notes: reproducible in staging when token-creation service omits parent_key_id header during minting.
logs:
Sample snippets from proxy/access logs (redacted):
2026-03-13T09:12:05Z | req_id=abc123 | token_id=ephemeral-7a2f | parent_key_id=NULL | X-Forwarded-For=35.201.22.11 | status=200 | latency=120ms
2026-03-13T09:12:06Z | req_id=abc124 | token_id=ephemeral-7a2f | parent_key_id=NULL | status=429 | quota_scope=tenant | X-RateLimit-Remaining=0
2026-03-13T09:12:07Z | req_id=abc125 | token_id=ephemeral-9b3c | parent_key_id=org-993 | status=200 | latency=95ms

Auth service trace (customer-provided):
- Token mint call returns ephemeral token with header `x-parent-key-id: org-993` in some flows but missing in rotated flow.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and diagnostics: 
- 2026-03-13 10:00 UTC: Support received report from NimbleDocs (CS AE: Marco Ruiz).
- 2026-03-13 10:12 UTC: Support captured request/response headers and observed parent_key_id null for many ephemeral tokens.
- 2026-03-13 11:00 UTC: Replicated in staging by removing parent_key propagation from token mint path — reproduced identical 429 pattern.
- Quota-service metrics show tokens with missing parent_id are being charged against a fallback accounting path that currently increments both user and tenant buckets for safety (legacy behavior introduced in 2024-auth-fallback change).
- Console refresh occasionally shows tenant quota increase (billing upgrade), but enforcement layer still uses in-memory token-bucket snapshots that lag ~30s under strong churn.

Hypothesis: 
1) Missing parent_key metadata on ephemeral tokens triggers fallback code path which increments both user and tenant counters to avoid orphaned tokens (legacy safety).
2) Combined with high concurrency and shard-snapshot lag, tenant bucket gets exhausted leading to 429s even though console shows nominal headroom.

Evidence: 
- Repro in staging with parent_key omitted.
- Quota-service logs show double increment events flagged with tag `legacy_fallback_charge`.

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Instructed customer to enable a minting path that ensures parent_key header is always set (workaround).
- Increased quota-service token refill smoothing temporarily for this org to reduce transient 429s.
resolution:
Short-term (applied 2026-03-14):
- Deployed hotfix to quota-service to stop double-incrementing when parent_key is missing; instead mark token as 'orphaned' and count only against user bucket until token is reconciled. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4021).
- Updated enforcement path to prefer persisted parent_key mapping in DB if header absent (failsafe).
- Released guidance to NimbleDocs: ensure token mint flow includes `x-parent-key-id` header; SDK patch v1.12.4 validates mint response.

Long-term actions (backlog / post-incident):
- Add robust instrumentation for fallback charge events across quota shards (owner: quota-team).
- Migrate legacy fallback behavior to a reconciliation job that runs asynchronously and does not increment tenant bucket synchronously. (TICKET: INT-3301).
- Improve console -> enforcement consistency with short-lived snapshot windows and write-through invalidation on billing changes.

Customer communication:
- Notified NimbleDocs 2026-03-14 09:10 UTC of hotfix and recommended steps. They confirmed reduced 429s in a 2-hour validation window.
